steps.text: Store clean drinking water in sealed containers above flood water level.
Pack essential medicines, dry rations, and personal identity documents in waterproof bags.
Move livestock, poultry, and valuable household belongings to higher elevated ground.
Locate your nearest designated community flood relief shelter and evacuation route.
Charge phones and power banks fully before electric power cuts occur.
Keep emergency battery torches, radios, and spare dry cells ready nearby.
Clear neighborhood drainage ditches and gutters to reduce localized water accumulation.
Save local district disaster control room helpline numbers on your phone.
Switch off your home main electricity breaker and cooking gas immediately.
Evacuate promptly to elevated shelters before flood water reaches your doorway.
Never walk or swim through flowing flood water of any depth.
Do not drive motor vehicles through submerged roads or washed bridges.
Stay away from fallen power cables and submerged electric transformers.
Use a strong wooden stick to test ground firmness when walking.
Move to upper building floors or elevated roofs if suddenly trapped.
Call national emergency helpline 112 immediately if trapped by rising water.
Return home only after local authorities declare flood waters fully receded.
Boil all drinking water vigorously for ten minutes before personal consumption.
Do not touch damp electrical appliances until certified dry and safe.
Watch carefully for snakes and dangerous wild animals inside damaged rooms.
Discard all food items that made contact with contaminated flood water.
Disinfect floor surfaces, water wells, and kitchen utensils using chlorine bleach.
Photograph property damages thoroughly before initiating repairs for relief claims.
Report blocked local drainage or missing persons to district emergency teams.
